full_judgment: 6. Mr. Anisul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of appellant Akhi Begum, submitted that none of the witnesses, who arrived at the scene of occurrence, in any way, implicated this appellant in the offence committed. He pointed out that only the victim and her mother, who was not an eyewitness, named this appellant as the person who took the victim to the room of Kabir Hossain and left her there. He submitted that it has not been alleged that the victim was in any way confined in that room. He submitted that, therefore, there cannot be any presumption that she knowingly took the victim to that room for any criminal purpose to be perpetrated by Kabir. He further submitted that there is no evidence that the appellant had any knowledge about the act or offence which might be committed by the principal accused and, therefore; she cannot be held liable for aiding and abetting in the offence alleged. He submits that there being absolutely no evidence on record to show any criminal intention on the part of this appellant, she is entitled to be acquitted.
